defect: Uses '#if GISMO_WITH_MPI' although the config defines the macro without a value, which breaks preprocessing or picks the wrong branch.
`#if GISMO_WITH_MPI` breaks compilation when MPI is enabled, because the macro is defined empty by #cmakedefine.
Replacing 'namespace helper' with 'namespace rtl { namespace io {' left the following stray '{' in place, which unbalances the namespaces and breaks compilation.
'namespace rtl { namespace io {' is followed by a stray '{' and the closing braces do not match, so the header fails to compile.
nPatches() now asserts that m_patches is a gsMultiPatch, and patch(i) calls it, so a field over a single geometry or other function set fails the assertion.
nPatches() now dynamic_casts to gsMultiPatch and asserts, so fields whose domain is a single gsGeometry fail; patch(i) now calls nPatches() and fails the same way.
markTagged push_backs indices without keeping m_tagged sorted and unique. is_tagged_index and the tagged index lookup binary-search that vector, so they give wrong results.
markTagged push_backs indices unsorted and possibly duplicated, but is_tagged_index uses std::binary_search on m_tagged, so tagged lookups give wrong answers.

fix_subject: fixed copy constructor for gsMesh fixed creation of gsParametrization<T>::createFlatMesh() such that the vertices of a face match the pointers of vertex
defect: The new copy constructor and assignment clone the faces and copy the edges, but these still point at the source mesh's vertices, leaving dangling or shared pointers.
The new copy constructor and assignment clone faces and copy edges, but their vertex pointers still point to the source mesh's vertices, giving dangling or aliased pointers.
The .hpp defines the members as non-template gsHalfEdgeMesh:: functions although the class is declared as template<class T>, so the code does not compile.
The .hpp defines members as non-template gsHalfEdgeMesh:: functions, while the header declares gsHalfEdgeMesh as a class template, so it does not compile.
Constructors initialize gsVector<T,2>/gsVector<T,3> which is not the base gsVector<T,dim>, failing on some compilers.
The constructors initialize the base as gsVector<T,2> and gsVector<T,3>, although the base class is gsVector<T,dim>, which is ill-formed and breaks the build on other compilers.
The file-scope macro DScalar is redefined as DScalar2<T,-1>, but T is undeclared outside a template, so the exprtk AD forward and adaptor headers fail to compile with GISMO_WITH_ADIFF.
'#define DScalar gismo::ad::DScalar2<T,-1>' is used at namespace scope in the exprtk AD headers, where T is undefined, so GISMO_WITH_ADIFF builds fail to compile.
reshape_expr checks dimensions in its constructor before they are valid, and eval returns a map over the temporary _u.eval(k), which dangles.
reshape_expr asserts on rows()*cols() in the constructor, where they are not yet known, and eval returns a gsAsMatrix view of a temporary _u.eval(k).
Removing GISMO_EXPORT from gsMpiComm leaves its out-of-line members unexported from the shared library (link errors).
GISMO_EXPORT was removed from gsMpiComm, so its symbols are not exported from the shared library (link errors on Windows and shared builds).
std::accumulate with int init 0 truncates the ply thicknesses (0.1 sums to 0), giving a wrong total thickness and mid-plane.
std::accumulate with int init 0 truncates the ply thicknesses (total thickness becomes 0), and reusing t_tot breaks the mid-plane and assert logic.
std::accumulate(_thickness..., 0) uses an int initial value, so the real ply thicknesses are truncated when summed; t_tot is also reused as the running sum.
std::accumulate(..., 0) with an int initial value truncates the sum of real thicknesses (0.1 becomes 0), so t_tot and z_mid are wrong.
The new interpolation routine has a wrong component condition (com!=-1 || r!=com skips everything), an empty const boundary matrix, wrong fixedDofs access and other errors.
gsDirichletValuesByInterpolation assigns to a const boundary matrix, has a wrong condition 'com!=-1 || r!=com', and mixes fixedDofs[com] and fixedDofs(com), so it cannot compile or work.

fix_subject: fixed double parametrization rotation function, modified in gsMultipatch the function which stores the interfaces and added function to reparametrize the patches in the vertices
defect: The coefficient-reversal loop runs to dimU*dimV-1, so the last coefficient row of mpar is never set.
In the 180-degree rotation, the loop runs to i < dimU*dimV-1, so the last coefficient row of mpar is never filled.
bc.geoMap() is called unconditionally, which asserts when no geometry map is set even for parametric Dirichlet data.
bc.geoMap() is fetched unconditionally at function start, which dereferences a null geometry map (later an assertion) when the boundary conditions are parametric and no geoMap is set.
fixedDofs is indexed as (ii,r) with u.dim() columns, but the mapper's bindex already includes the component, so values are written into the wrong layout and column.
fixedDofs is sized boundarySize x u.dim() and indexed (ii,r), but bindex(...,k,r) already returns an index across all components, so the multi-column layout is wrong and can index out of bounds.

fix_subject: fix std::bind and use int for shorts
defect: The GS_BIND2ND definitions are swapped: the C++11+ branch uses std::bind2nd (removed in C++17), and the pre-C++11 branch uses std::bind with an unqualified placeholders.
GS_BIND2ND is swapped between branches: the C++11 branch uses std::bind2nd and the pre-C++11 branch uses std::bind with an unqualified placeholders::_1.

fix_subject: fixed assembling problem (RHS nultiplied for the wrong factor)
defect: The new right-hand-side transformation multiplies rhsVals by detG*sqrtDetG_inv, a wrong factor.
The added scaling of the right-hand side by detG*sqrtDetG_inv multiplies it by the wrong factor, because the quadrature weight already includes the measure.
The include `gsAssembler/gsLinpLapAssembler.h` has the wrong case; the file is gsLinPLapAssembler.h, so the build fails on case-sensitive filesystems.
The new include `gsAssembler/gsLinpLapAssembler.h` gets the case wrong; the file is `gsLinPLapAssembler.h`, so the build fails on case-sensitive filesystems.
The onormal expression lost rowVar/colVar, and rowSpan/colSpan now raise GISMO_ERROR instead of returning false, so any use of the outer normal in an assembled expression fails.
onormal_expr::rowSpan/colSpan were changed to GISMO_ERROR and rowVar/colVar were removed, so any expression using nv() fails at run time or does not compile.
isBoundaryElement hard-codes indices 0 and 1, so it reads out of bounds for D=1 and ignores further directions for D>2 in a class templated on D.
isBoundaryElement hard-codes indices 0 and 1 in a domain iterator templated on dimension D, so 1D reads out of bounds and 3D misses the z faces.
The return type is misspelled as gsGeometr, and an undeclared componentBasis is used, so the code does not compile.
The new gsGeometry::component uses the misspelled return type 'typename gsGeometr::uPtr' and the undefined name componentBasis, so it does not compile.
The 'some high value' tolerance was changed from math::pow(10,8)=1e8 to 1e-8, so inexact cases fail the check.
The fallback tolerance meant as 'some high value' (previously 10^8) was rewritten as 1e-8, a tiny value.
gsSpectraGenSymShiftSolver always uses SpectraShiftOps with opB(B). Buckling mode needs B-op = A, so it computes with the wrong operator.
gsSpectraGenSymShiftSolver accepts a GEigsMode parameter, but SpectraShiftOps always builds B as the B-matrix product, so Buckling mode, which needs A as the B operator, gives wrong eigenvalues.
unrefineElements_withCoefs/withTransfer compute transfer(OX) from the old, finer basis to the new, coarser one, which is not a valid refinement transfer, so the coefficients come out wrong.
unrefineElements_withCoefs multiplies the coefficients by transfer(OX), the old-to-new transfer, but after unrefinement the old basis is finer, so the coarse coefficients come out wrong.
Adds an L2 mass term to the local matrix in the branch where L2approx is false, corrupting the biharmonic system.
A mass (L2) term was added to the biharmonic stiffness matrix in the branch where L2approx is false, so the wrong operator is assembled for an unchanged right-hand side.

fix_subject: fix eval_into: now for different dofs and points
defect: result is sized like the patch basis actives, but each column receives map^T*beval whose length is the number of mapped dofs, which can differ per point.
eval_into sizes result like the source basis actives (bact) and assigns map^T*beval per column, but the number of mapped actives can differ, giving a size mismatch or out-of-bounds write.

fix_subject: Fix evaluation of derivatives in gsMappedSpline

The new deriv2_into calls deriv_into instead of deriv2_into and sizes the result with S from targetDim instead of domainDim, so second derivatives are wrong.

fix_subject: fix eval_into: now for different dofs and points
defect: active_into writes each sub-basis block at row offset 'shift', the dof-index shift, instead of the accumulated row count. That writes out of bounds or places rows wrongly.
active_into writes each block at row offset 'shift' (the cumulative basis size) instead of the cumulative number of active rows, so it writes out of bounds or into the wrong rows.

The uniform sample grid uses i/n, so the parameters never reach the boundary value 1.
The 'offset == 1' block appends the same corner boundary indices a second time, producing duplicate entries.
For offset==1 the 'DIRTY AND QUICK' block appends the same corner boundary indices a second time, duplicating DoFs.

A non-inline operator<< is defined in a header, so including it in more than one translation unit causes multiple-definition link errors.
